answers.explanation: The endpoint is POST /process/file and receives form_data.file_id, form_data.collection_name, and optional form_data.content. Its dependency is get_verified_user, which only accepts users whose role is user or admin; the displayed dependency source shows that other roles are rejected. The displayed get_current_user source shows token extraction and JWT/API-key authentication, but the exact helper relationships for decode_token and get_current_user_by_api_key remain unresolved in the current interpretation. After authentication, the endpoint authorizes the input file differently by role: an admin calls Files.get_file_by_id(form_data.file_id), while a non-admin calls Files.get_file_by_id_and_user_id(form_data.file_id, user.id). Thus a caller-owned file is eligible for a non-admin when that user-scoped lookup returns it; another user's file is not returned by that non-admin lookup and the endpoint reaches its 404 NOT_FOUND branch. An admin can retrieve a file by ID without the displayed user-id restriction. The supplied collection_name is copied to the local collection_name, or defaults to file-{file.id} when omitted. The displayed endpoint performs no visible ownership or permission check tying collection_name to the caller or to the file owner. If content is supplied, it first attempts to delete file-{file.id} (not the supplied destination collection), then builds a document from the supplied content. If content is absent and collection_name is supplied, it reads the existing file-{file.id} vector collection and otherwise builds a document from the file's stored content. If neither content nor collection_name is supplied, it processes the file path or stored content. The eventual save call passes the constructed docs, the supplied/default collection_name, metadata containing file.id, filename, and hash, add=True when form_data.collection_name is truthy and False otherwise, and the authenticated user. On a truthy result, the endpoint records collection_name on the same file record, marks that file completed, stores the hash, and returns success; on failure it marks that same file failed and clears its hash. Therefore the input authorization object is the file selected by file_id, and the endpoint's own post-success database updates also affect that same file. The vector destination, however, is the independent collection_name string supplied by the caller (or the file-derived default); the displayed code does not establish that the caller owns it or that it is the same object as the authorized file. The actual authorization behavior inside save_docs_to_vector_db and the vector database's collection-level access controls are not displayed, so cross-user effects at the vector layer remain unresolved rather than being assumed allowed or denied.

paths.explanation: When the required authentication token is absent, the displayed authentication source raises 401 before process_file runs. This path is source-supported, but the broader authentication helper closure is not fully interpreted.

For an authenticated API-key path, get_current_user_by_api_key visibly checks that API keys are enabled, that non-admin users have the features.api_keys permission, and, when endpoint restrictions are enabled, that the request path matches an allowed configured path. It returns the user if those checks pass. The current source interpretation has not linked this helper to the actual call in get_current_user, so the path is behaviorally supported by displayed source but has an unresolved caller/helper linkage. After get_verified_user, the file lookup is user-scoped for non-admins and unrestricted by user ID for admins. The destination collection ownership and save-layer authorization are not shown.

policy.text: An authenticated and verified caller may enter the endpoint only if the applicable authentication and API-key restrictions pass; file access remains role-dependent.

paths.explanation: For JWT authentication, the displayed source decodes the token, optionally validates its jti, loads the user by the token subject, and rejects invalid or missing users. get_verified_user then permits only user or admin roles. The current interpretation has not linked the displayed decode_token helper to the actual call, so token-helper closure remains a source gap. Once inside process_file, non-admin access is limited to a file returned by the user-id-constrained lookup; another user's file therefore follows the visible not-found behavior. Admin access uses ID-only lookup. The destination collection is passed onward without a visible caller-ownership check, while save_docs_to_vector_db and its underlying vector authorization are out of scope of the displayed source.

policy.text: A valid verified JWT caller may process an authorized input file, subject to the role-specific lookup and any opaque downstream vector authorization.

answers.explanation: The visible caller is POST /process/file, whose dependency is get_verified_user. Authentication first obtains a token from the authorization credential, token cookie, or request state; no token raises 401. API-key tokens call get_current_user_by_api_key, which looks up the user, requires API keys to be enabled (and for non-admins the features.api_keys permission), and, when configured, requires the request path to match an allowed endpoint. Other tokens call decode_token, optionally validate jti, and load the user by the token id; invalid, missing, or mismatched users are rejected. get_verified_user then permits only roles user and admin. These helper calls are now visible in the displayed source, but the current accepted interpretation retains an unresolved semantic-link diagnostic for those helper relationships, so authentication closure is not treated as fully verified by this result. After authentication, process_file uses Files.get_file_by_id(file_id) for an admin and Files.get_file_by_id_and_user_id(file_id,user.id) for a non-admin. A caller-owned file can therefore proceed for a non-admin if the user-scoped lookup returns it; another user's file does not return through that lookup and reaches the visible 404 NOT_FOUND branch. An admin uses the ID-only lookup. The local collection_name is the submitted value, or file-{file.id} when omitted. No visible check ties the submitted collection_name to the caller, to the file owner, or to the authorized file. The endpoint builds documents from submitted content, an existing file-{file.id} vector collection, or the file path/stored content depending on the visible content and collection_name branches. It then calls save_docs_to_vector_db with the docs, collection_name, file metadata including file.id, add=True only when the submitted collection_name is truthy, and the authenticated user. If that call returns truthy, the endpoint updates collection_name, status, and hash on the same file selected by file_id and returns success. If processing or saving fails, it marks that same file failed and clears its hash, then returns a 400 except for the specific pandoc error. If BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is enabled, it updates the selected file's content/status/hash and returns without the vector save. Thus the input authorization object and the endpoint's own database object are the selected file, while the vector destination is an independent collection identifier and is not shown to be the same object. Whether save_docs_to_vector_db or the vector backend authorizes or rejects writing to another user's collection is not displayed, so cross-user vector effects remain unresolved rather than being assumed allowed or denied.
